claim: The MiMIC collection comprises 7434 insertions in 7400 lines associated with 4367 genes.
source: In total, the collection comprises 7434 insertions in 7400 lines associated with 4367 genes; 34 lines contain two insertions each.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a summary of the collection.

claim: The MiMIC collection includes 2854 insertions in coding introns of 1862 distinct genes.
source: As shown in Figure 1B we selected a total of 2854 MiMIC insertions in coding introns of 1862 distinct genes for inclusion in the GDP collection.
evidence: This is directly stated in the text and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: 1732 insertions are in constitutive coding introns that permit tagging of all annotated protein isoforms (Gold set).
source: The collection includes 1732 insertions in constitutive coding introns that permit tagging of all annotated protein isoforms (Gold set), 814 insertions in alternative coding introns that permit tagging of more than 50% of annotated protein isoforms (Silver set), and 328 insertions in alternative coding that permit tagging of less than 50% of annotated protein isoforms (Bronze set).
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the text describing the collection composition.

claim: 814 insertions are in alternative coding introns that permit tagging of more than 50% of annotated protein isoforms (Silver set).
source: The collection includes 1732 insertions in constitutive coding introns that permit tagging of all annotated protein isoforms (Gold set), 814 insertions in alternative coding introns that permit tagging of more than 50% of annotated protein isoforms (Silver set), and 328 insertions in alternative coding that permit tagging of less than 50% of annotated protein isoforms (Bronze set).
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the text describing the collection composition.

claim: 328 insertions are in alternative coding introns that permit tagging of less than 50% of annotated protein isoforms (Bronze set).
source: The collection includes 1732 insertions in constitutive coding introns that permit tagging of all annotated protein isoforms (Gold set), 814 insertions in alternative coding introns that permit tagging of more than 50% of annotated protein isoforms (Silver set), and 328 insertions in alternative coding that permit tagging of less than 50% of annotated protein isoforms (Bronze set).
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the text describing the collection composition.

claim: A library of 400 GFP-tagged genes was created from the MiMIC collection.
source: They allowed us to create a library of 400 GFP-tagged genes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a key result.

claim: 72% of internally tagged proteins are functional.
source: We show that 72% of internally tagged proteins are functional, and that more than 90% can be imaged in unfixed tissues.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a key finding.

claim: More than 90% of tagged proteins can be imaged in unfixed tissues.
source: We show that 72% of internally tagged proteins are functional, and that more than 90% can be imaged in unfixed tissues.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a key finding.

claim: MiMIC insertions in coding introns in the gene trap orientation are 92% mutagenic.
source: Our data show that 92% of MiMICs inserted in a coding intron in the gene trap configuration are highly mutagenic and function as gene traps, while 100% of those that are in the opposite configuration are not mutagenic.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion based on the data presented.

claim: 100% of MiMIC insertions in the opposite (non-gene trap) configuration are not mutagenic.
source: Our data show that 92% of MiMICs inserted in a coding intron in the gene trap configuration are highly mutagenic and function as gene traps, while 100% of those that are in the opposite configuration are not mutagenic.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion based on the data presented.

claim: 58 out of 63 MiMIC insertions in the correct gene trap orientation cause homozygous lethality and fail to complement null alleles or deficiencies.
source: The MiMIC insertions in coding introns of 63 of the 114 essential genes are inserted in the correct orientation to function as gene traps, and 58 of these 63 cause homozygous lethality and fail to complement null alleles or deficiencies (Figure 1—source data 2) that delete the target gene (Figure 1—source data 1); hence, MiMIC is highly mutagenic.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with reference to source data.

claim: MiMIC functions as designed in 109 out of 114 insertion lines.
source: In summary, our data show that MiMIC functions as designed in 109/114 insertion lines, and is thus a highly reliable gene trap.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the gene trap functionality data.

claim: The success rate of obtaining at least one insertion in the correct orientation via RMCE is 66%.
source: The success rate of obtaining at least one insertion in the correct orientation is currently 133/200 or 66%.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section.

claim: Upon reinjection, the RMCE success rate is 62%.
source: Upon reinjection we obtained a 62% success rate.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section.

claim: With two injections of about 500 embryos each, approximately 175 out of 200 properly tagged genes can be derived.
source: Hence, with two injections of about 500 embryos each we derived ∼175/200 properly tagged genes.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section.

claim: The lethality of 42 out of 58 lethal gene trap lines was reverted (72%) upon tagging.
source: The lethality of 42 out of 58 lethal gene trap lines was reverted (72%) upon tagging.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section.

claim: 72% to 77% of proteins tagged at various internal locations retain function or are not severely affected.
source: Hence, our data indicate that 72% (42/58) to 77% (88/114) of proteins tagged at various internal locations retain function or are not severely affected (Figure 1C and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with reference to figure and source data.

claim: Insertion of a tag within known, conserved protein domains is more likely to disrupt protein function.
source: In summary, insertion of a tag within known, conserved protein domains is more likely to disrupt protein function, and inserting an artificial exon that encodes a tag is effective and not disruptive in 77% of the proteins tested.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the analysis of tag insertion sites relative to protein domains.

claim: Of the 88 tagged essential genes that retain protein function, 26 tags are inserted within annotated protein domains and 62 are not inserted within an annotated protein domain.
source: Of the 88 tagged essential genes that retain protein function, 26 tags are inserted within annotated protein domains and 62 are not inserted within an annotated protein domain (χ2, p = 0.0001).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with statistical analysis.

claim: For internal tags that disrupt essential proteins, 14 tags are inserted within annotated domains vs 12 inserted within unannotated sequences.
source: However, we found no such bias for internal tags that disrupt essential proteins: 14 tags inserted within annotated domains vs 12 inserted within unannotated sequences (χ2, p = 0.7).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with statistical analysis.

claim: EGFP expression can be detected in CNS of 84% (168/200) of tagged genes in third instar larvae.
source: To determine what fraction of our set of 200 proteins are expressed in the CNS of third instar larvae, we performed immunostaining with anti-GFP antibodies and detected EGFP expression in 168/200 lines (84%).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section.

claim: EGFP expression was observed in adult brain in 11 out of 32 lines (6% of total analyzed lines) that did not show detectable expression in larval CNS.
source: The lines that did not show detectable expression in larval CNS were tested for expression in adult brain, and EGFP expression was observed in 11/32 lines (6% of total analyzed lines).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section.

claim: EGFP fluorescence in unfixed brains was detected in 38 of 40 randomly selected lines.
source: To further establish what fraction of the expression patterns could be monitored using unfixed tissue, we compared anti-GFP stained third instar larval brains with unfixed brains in 40 randomly selected lines. We were able to detect expression of EGFP fluorescence in unfixed brains in 38 of 40 lines.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section.

claim: The tagged α-Cat protein localizes to adherens junctions as previously reported for α-Cat.
source: The tagged protein is ubiquitously expressed in the eye disc and localizes to adherens junctions as previously reported for α-Cat (Sarpal et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with citation to previous work.

claim: A single anti-α-Cat reaction band of 100 kDa is detected in y w flies.
source: A single anti-α-Cat reaction band of 100 kDa is detected in y w flies, whereas y w; α-Cat-EGFP-α-Cat extracts show a single band of about 135 kDa, in agreement with the estimated molecular weight (MW) of 35 kDa for the protein tag (Figure 4C, left).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with reference to Figure 4C.

claim: y w; α-Cat-EGFP-α-Cat extracts show a single band of about 135 kDa.
source: A single anti-α-Cat reaction band of 100 kDa is detected in y w flies, whereas y w; α-Cat-EGFP-α-Cat extracts show a single band of about 135 kDa, in agreement with the estimated molecular weight (MW) of 35 kDa for the protein tag (Figure 4C, left).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with reference to Figure 4C.

claim: The estimated molecular weight of the protein tag is 35 kDa.
source: A single anti-α-Cat reaction band of 100 kDa is detected in y w flies, whereas y w; α-Cat-EGFP-α-Cat extracts show a single band of about 135 kDa, in agreement with the estimated molecular weight (MW) of 35 kDa for the protein tag (Figure 4C, left).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section.

claim: The vast majority of α-Cat protein is tagged, with no detectable untagged protein in homozygous tagged animals.
source: Hence, we are not able to detect untagged protein in homozygous tagged animals, indicating that the vast majority protein is tagged, but we cannot exclude that some protein in not tagged.

claim: y w; α-Cat-EGFP-α-Cat flies expressing deGradFP and kept at 18°C are viable.
source: Interestingly, y w; α-Cat-EGFP-α-Cat flies expressing deGradFP and kept at 18°C are viable, whereas animals kept at 28°C, to express deGradFP, are embryonic lethal (Sarpal et al., 2012).

claim: Both deGradFP and iGFPi knockdown experiments cause a rough eye phenotype.

claim: iGFPi results in a more severe eye phenotype than deGradFP for α-Cat knockdown.
source: Both knockdown experiments cause a rough eye phenotype: however iGFPi results in a more severe phenotype (Figure 4D-b).

claim: Homozygous y w dlg1-EGFP-dlg1 flies are viable and do not exhibit obvious phenotypes.
source: Homozygous y w dlg1-EGFP-dlg1 flies are viable and do not exhibit obvious phenotypes, indicating that the tagged Dlg1 is able to function normally.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section.

claim: Western blots with anti GFP show a nearly identical banding pattern for Dlg1, demonstrating that exon skipping is not occurring at a detectable level.
source: Westerns with anti GFP show a nearly identical banding pattern in these flies, demonstrating that exon skipping is not occurring at a detectable level when assessed with western blots (Figure 5B, bottom blot).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with reference to Figure 5B.

claim: y w dlg1-EGFP-dlg1;UAS-deGradFP/tub-GAL4 flies raised at 18°C develop normally and eclose without obvious phenotype.
source: The y w dlg1-EGFP-dlg1;UAS-deGradFP/tub-GAL4 flies raised at 18°C develop normally and eclose without obvious phenotype.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section.

source: In contrast, embryos that are raised continuously at 28°C are embryonic lethal, an earlier lethal phase than dlg1 null mutants, which are third instar lethal.

claim: dlg1 null mutants are third instar lethal.
source: In contrast, embryos that are raised continuously at 28°C are embryonic lethal, an earlier lethal phase than dlg1 null mutants, which are third instar lethal.

claim: Germ line clones of dlg1 null alleles are embryonic lethal.
source: However, in zygotic null mutants, there is a large maternal component of Dlg1 (Woods and Bryant, 1991), and germ line clones of dlg1 null alleles are embryonic lethal (Perrimon, 1988), suggesting that the maternally deposited protein is degraded in y w dlg1-EGFP-dlg1; UAS-deGradFP/tub-GAL4 animals grown at 28°C.

claim: The maternally deposited Dlg1 protein is degraded in y w dlg1-EGFP-dlg1; UAS-deGradFP/tub-GAL4 animals grown at 28°C.

claim: Both iGFPi and deGradFP knockdown result in a complete loss of on- and off-transients in electroretinograms (ERGs).
source: In agreement with the phenotype of a brp severe loss of function mutation in photoreceptors, we observe a complete loss of on- and off-transients (Figure 6D-b,c) in electroretinograms (ERGs) using both iGFPi and deGradFP knockdown, indicating severe synaptic transmission defects of photoreceptors.

claim: Both iGFPi and deGradFP knockdown result in a 50% reduction in ERG amplitude.

claim: Brp might play a role in eye development or the visual transduction pathway.
source: We also observe a 50% reduction in ERG amplitude in both experiments, suggesting that Brp might play a role in eye development or the visual transduction pathway (Figure 6D-b,c).

claim: deGradFP knockdown efficiency is pronounced at NMJs in larvae that were kept at 28°C for 18–22 hr.
source: deGradFP knockdown efficiency is pronounced at NMJs in larvae that were kept at 28°C for 18–22 hr, as gauged by immunostaining with anti Brp (nc82) (Figure 7A-b) and anti GFP (data not shown).

claim: Larvae kept at 28°C for 18–24 hr have EJP amplitudes that are reduced by 76% compared to animals kept at 18°C.

evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with reference to Figure 7A.

claim: An 18 hr period of deGradFP expression at 28°C during third larval instar development is sufficient to remove most of the Brp-EGFP-Brp protein and cause severe loss of function phenotypes.
source: In summary, an 18 hr period of deGradFP expression at 28°C during third larval instar development is sufficient to remove most of the Brp-EGFP-Brp protein and cause severe loss of function phenotypes.

claim: iGFPi is not as efficient as deGradFP at some stages of development or in some tissues for Brp knockdown.
source: These data suggest that iGFPi is not as efficient as deGradFP at some stages of development or in some tissues, possibly because the Brp protein has a very long half-life and is less affected by depletion of mRNA levels by iGFPi than by degradation of the protein by deGradFP.

claim: The Brp protein possibly has a very long half-life.
source: These data suggest that iGFPi is not as efficient as deGradFP at some stages of development or in some tissues, possibly because the Brp protein has a very long half-life and is less affected by depletion of mRNA levels by iGFPi than by degradation of the protein by deGradFP.

claim: Protein expression of Roughest and NetrinA is restored to a level comparable to larvae that were never exposed to the restrictive temperature after returning to 18°C for 24 hr.

claim: The Dnc-EGFP-Dnc protein is expressed in the adult brain and is mostly restricted to mushroom bodies (MB).
source: The Dnc-EGFP-Dnc protein is expressed in the adult brain and is mostly restricted to mushroom bodies (MB), the center for learning and memory in Drosophila (Figure 9B).

claim: The fusion protein is expressed in all MB lobes (α, α′, β, β′ and γ) in the adult brain.
source: A more detailed analysis reveals that the fusion protein is expressed in all MB lobes (α, α′, β, β′ and γ) in the adult brain (Figure 9B), and the GFP staining reveals a much crisper expression pattern than the anti Dunce antibody (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A) (Nighorn et al., 1991).

claim: After 48 hr at 28°C, Dnc-EGFP-Dnc could not or barely be detected.

claim: Dnc-EGFP-Dnc protein expression is restored 48 hr after a shift back to 18°C.

evidence: This is stated directly in the results section.

claim: EGFP expression can easily be detected in the brain, muscles, imaginal discs, salivary gland nuclei, ovaries, and testis.
source: As shown in Figure 2A, GFP expression can easily be detected in the brain (Rab3 interacting molecule: Rim), muscles (Myosin Heavy Chain: MHC), imaginal discs (Abl tyrosine kinase: Abl), salivary gland nuclei (CrebA), ovaries (oo18 RNA-binding protein: orb), and testis (Syncrip), in agreement with published expression data (Lantz et al., 1994; Fogerty et al., 1999; Abrams and Andrew, 2005; Graf et al., 2012; McDermott et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with reference to Figure 2A and citations.

claim: Localization studies for Delta (Dl) and Ecdysone Receptor (EcR) show a precise colocalization of EGFP and the protein specific antibodies.
source: Moreover, localization studies for Delta (Dl) and Ecdysone Receptor (EcR) show a precise colocalization of EGFP and the protein specific antibodies for Delta and EcR, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Proteins localize to the proper subcellular compartments as shown for Catalase (cytoplasmic or organelle associated), Hmx (nuclear), and dpr15 (membrane associated).
source: Finally, proteins localize to the proper subcellular compartments as shown in Figure 2B for a cytoplasmic or organelle present in cytoplasm associated (Catalase), nuclear (H6-like-homeobox: Hmx) and membrane associated protein (dpr15) (Figure 2B) (Beard and Holtzman, 1987; Hofmann et al., 2010; Özkan et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with reference to Figure 2B and citations.

claim: The EGFP patterns faithfully report expression and protein distribution.
source: These examples indicate that the EGFP patterns faithfully report expression and protein distribution.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the expression pattern analysis.

claim: The expression patterns in unfixed tissue generally match the pattern observed by GFP antibody staining.
source: Although the expression patterns in each case generally matched the pattern observed by GFP antibody staining (Figure 3), the fluorescence intensity is often lower in unfixed tissue.

claim: The fluorescence intensity is often lower in unfixed tissue compared to antibody staining.
source: Although the expression patterns in each case generally matched the pattern observed by GFP antibody staining (Figure 3), the fluorescence intensity is often lower in unfixed tissue.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section.

claim: Most internally tagged proteins are present at levels that permit imaging in unfixed tissue.
source: These data show that most internally tagged proteins are present at levels that permit imaging in unfixed tissue.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the unfixed tissue imaging experiments.

claim: There are three GFP RNAi transgenic lines available that express different short hairpin RNAs (shRNA) against the EGFP tag under the control of the UAS/GAL4 system.
source: There are three GFP RNAi transgenic lines available and each expresses a different short hairpin RNA (shRNA) against the EGFP tag under the control of the UAS/GAL4 system to knock down the expression of GFP-tagged genes (Neumüller et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with citation.

claim: No off-target effects have been documented for GFP RNAi.
source: There are two important advantages of GFP RNAi over gene-specific RNAi: no off-target effects have been documented and a single set of highly selective and efficient GFP shRNAs can be used to knock down the expression of any tagged gene.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section.

claim: A single set of highly selective and efficient GFP shRNAs can be used to knock down the expression of any tagged gene.
source: There are two important advantages of GFP RNAi over gene-specific RNAi: no off-target effects have been documented and a single set of highly selective and efficient GFP shRNAs can be used to knock down the expression of any tagged gene.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section.

claim: deGradFP is an ubiquitination-based system in which the F-Box domain of the Slmb protein N-terminus is fused to a single-chain nanoantibody fragment (vhhGFP4) that recognizes the GFP tag.
source: Alternatively, a GFP tagged protein can be degraded using the deGradFP system developed by Caussinus et al. (2011). deGradFP is an ubiquitination-based system in which the F-Box domain of the Slmb protein N-terminus is fused to a single-chain nanoantibody fragment (vhhGFP4) that recognizes the GFP tag.

claim: The deGradFP system uses the host ubiquitination machinery to target GFP-tagged proteins for proteasomal degradation.
source: The system uses the host ubiquitination machinery to target GFP-tagged proteins for proteasomal degradation.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section.

source: This protein plays a critical role at the plasma membrane where it acts as an essential physical linker between the cadherin-β-catenin complex and the actin cytoskeleton (Desai et al., 2013).

source: The homozygous EGFP tagged gene is viable and displays no obvious phenotypes.

claim: α-Cat null mutants are embryonic lethal.
source: Because α-Cat null mutants are embryonic lethal (Sarpal et al., 2012), and its loss specifically in the eye (Seppa et al., 2008) or ovaries (Desai et al., 2013) is associated with severe developmental or cellular defects, the tagged protein must be functional.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with citation.

claim: Loss of α-Cat specifically in the eye or ovaries is associated with severe developmental or cellular defects.
source: Because α-Cat null mutants are embryonic lethal (Sarpal et al., 2012), and its loss specifically in the eye (Seppa et al., 2008) or ovaries (Desai et al., 2013) is associated with severe developmental or cellular defects, the tagged protein must be functional.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with citations.

claim: The tagged α-Cat protein must be functional.
source: Because α-Cat null mutants are embryonic lethal (Sarpal et al., 2012), and its loss specifically in the eye (Seppa et al., 2008) or ovaries (Desai et al., 2013) is associated with severe developmental or cellular defects, the tagged protein must be functional.

claim: The tagged α-Cat protein localizes to the proper intracellular domain, similar to the wild type protein.
source: The signals from each antibody colocalize and the tagged α-Cat protein localizes to the proper intracellular domain, similar to the wild type protein (Figure 3D-a; data not shown).

claim: The GAL4 system exhibits some temperature dependency due to the presence of an hsp70 promoter upstream of GAL4.
source: The GAL4 system exhibits some temperature dependency due to the presence of an hsp70 promoter upstream of GAL4 (Duffy, 2002).

source: GAL4 is expressed at low levels at 18°C, while expression is elevated at 28°C.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section.

source: We tested this and show that with the act-GAL4 driver, the temperature sensitive expression of GAL4 is quite pronounced (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).

claim: Knockdown with deGradFP causes rough eyes similar to one previously reported RNAi phenotype and knockdown using the α-Cat specific RNAi, FBst0033430.
source: Knockdown with deGradFP causes rough eyes similar to one previously reported RNAi phenotype (Seppa et al., 2008) and knockdown using the α-Cat specific RNAi, FBst0033430 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2-a), but is less severe than other two unpublished RNAi phenotypes (FBst0038987 and FBst0038197), both of which are pupal lethal when raised at 28°C (Figure 4—figure supplement 2-b–c).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with reference to figures and citation.

claim: deGradFP knockdown of α-Cat is less severe than two other unpublished RNAi phenotypes (FBst0038987 and FBst0038197), both of which are pupal lethal when raised at 28°C.
source: Knockdown with deGradFP causes rough eyes similar to one previously reported RNAi phenotype (Seppa et al., 2008) and knockdown using the α-Cat specific RNAi, FBst0033430 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2-a), but is less severe than other two unpublished RNAi phenotypes (FBst0038987 and FBst0038197), both of which are pupal lethal when raised at 28°C (Figure 4—figure supplement 2-b–c).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with reference to figures.

claim: Both tag-mediated knockdown strategies are effective at reducing gene function but may not cause null phenotypes.
source: Thus both tag-mediated knockdown strategies are effective at reducing gene function but, may not cause null phenotypes.

claim: Null mutations in discs large 1 (dlg1) cause larval lethality, oversized imaginal discs and brains in third instar larvae, and defects in neuromuscular junction development.
source: Null mutations in discs large 1 (dlg1) cause larval lethality, oversized imaginal discs and brains in third instar larvae, and defects in neuromuscular junction development (Stewart et al., 1972; Perrimon, 1988; Woods and Bryant, 1991; Woods et al., 1996; Budnik et al., 2006; Zhang et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with citations.

claim: The dlg1 locus contains 16 long isoforms and five approximately 24 kDa isoforms, the latter of which may not encode functional proteins.
source: The dlg1 locus contains 16 long isoforms and five approximately 24 kDa isoforms, the latter of which may not encode functional proteins (Mendoza-Topaz et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with citation.

claim: The MI06353 insertion permits tagging of all the long, presumably functional Dlg1 isoforms.
source: The MI06353 insertion is in an ideal location as it permits tagging of all the long, presumably functional Dlg1 isoforms.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section.

claim: The EGFP insertion site in dlg1 is located between protein domains and is less likely to interfere with normal protein function.
source: The EGFP insertion site is located between protein domains and is less likely to interfere with normal protein function (Figure 5A; Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with reference to figures.

claim: In zygotic null mutants of dlg1, there is a large maternal component of Dlg1.
source: However, in zygotic null mutants, there is a large maternal component of Dlg1 (Woods and Bryant, 1991), and germ line clones of dlg1 null alleles are embryonic lethal (Perrimon, 1988), suggesting that the maternally deposited protein is degraded in y w dlg1-EGFP-dlg1; UAS-deGradFP/tub-GAL4 animals grown at 28°C.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with citation.

claim: A mild decrease in NMJ growth in terms of bouton number and synapse complexity is observed in temperature shifted dlg1 knockdown animals compared to unshifted controls.
source: We also detect a mild decrease in NMJ growth in terms of bouton number and synapse complexity in the temperature shifted animals compared to unshifted controls (Figure 5D-a,d-white arrows, data not shown), consistent with dlg1 loss of function (Zhang et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with reference to figure and citation.

claim: The decrease in Dlg1-EGFP-Dlg1 in the muscle is far less robust compared with other tissues, such as the brain.
source: However, the decrease in Dlg1-EGFP-Dlg1 in the muscle is far less robust compared with other tissues, such as the brain, because the Tubulin driver leads to stronger expression in the brain compared to third instar larval muscles (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section.

claim: y w dlg1-EGFP-dlg1; UAS-deGradFP/tub-GAL4 animals shifted to 28°C as first instar larvae have defects in cell morphology and organization as observed in the larval midgut.
source: In addition to hyperproliferation, y w dlg1-EGFP-dlg1; UAS-deGradFP/tub-GAL4 animals shifted to 28°C as first instar larvae, much like dlg1 zygotic mutants, also have defects in cell morphology and organization as observed in the larval midgut compared to animals raised at 18°C (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: deGradFP not only prevents zygotic expression of Dlg1, but also eliminates maternal deposited Dlg1.
source: Taken together, these data show that deGradFP not only prevents zygotic expression of Dlg1, but also eliminates maternal deposited Dlg1, thus recapitulating phenotypes associated with zygotic null mutations and the lethality associated with mutant germ line clones.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the dlg1 knockdown experiments.

source: Bruchpilot (Brp) is a functional homolog of the human presynaptic protein ELKS/CAST/ERC (Wagh et al., 2006).

source: It is essential for assembly of active zones, Ca2+ channel clustering at NMJs, and release of neurotransmitters.

claim: brp null mutants show loss of presynaptic dense projections and severe defects in synaptic transmission.
source: brp null mutants show loss of presynaptic dense projections and severe defects in synaptic transmission (Kittel et al., 2006).

claim: MI02987 tags all but one annotated brp transcript.

source: ey-GAL4 drives expression in pupal and adult photoreceptors, lamina and medulla neurons, mushroom body neurons and other adult neurons (Sheng et al., 1997).
